question.skill_title: OIS vs Euribor swaps, discounting and tenor basis
question.stem:
EUR curves, 30Y: IRS (6M Euribor) 2.780%, ESTR OIS 2.732% (IRS - OIS = +4.8bp; part of this is accrual convention: OIS is ACT/360, the IRS fixed leg 30E/360).
You pay fixed on €200m 30Y IRS and receive fixed on €197m 30Y OIS, sized to be DV01-neutral. 'The IRS-OIS spread' means IRS rate minus OIS rate.

options: Flat risk: it is DV01-neutral so no market move matters
Long the IRS-OIS spread: it gains if the spread widens
Directional: it gains if rates fall regardless of the spread
Short the IRS-OIS spread: it gains if the spread narrows

result.expected: B. Long the IRS-OIS spread: it gains if the spread widens
result.why: Paying fixed in the IRS (and receiving OIS) gains when the IRS rate rises against OIS: long the spread. Receiving the IRS and paying OIS is the opposite: short the spread.

solution: The IRS DV01 is -€405.9k/bp; the OIS leg (€197m, +€405.9k/bp) offsets it.
A move of the IRS rate alone is a move in the spread: first-order +€811.7k (= -(+2) x -€405.9k); full revaluation +€811.7k.
IRS-OIS is the Euribor-ESTR basis. It widens when term/credit premium in Euribor rises vs overnight funding.
Because the OIS notional differs slightly from the IRS notional for the same DV01, 'equal notional' is NOT quite DV01-neutral (ACT/360 vs 30E/360 accrual).
